info.description:
Group Health and Benefits Data. Solved.
---
This is the API for Dart Health's [Data Nexus](https://www.darthealth.com/product). It supports benefits Administrators, Providers, Employers, and Analysts who need to manage real-time information for eligible Program Members.

In order to authenticate your API requests, please include your API key in the header:

```
authorization: apikey YOURAPIKEYHERE
```

## Client libraries:

### Ruby

A Ruby client is maintained for this API, the [`data_nexus`](https://rubygems.org/gems/data_nexus) gem, with its source at [github.com/DartHealth/datanexus-ruby](https://github.com/DartHealth/datanexus-ruby). It is optional, as every endpoint also works over plain HTTP. It handles:
  * the `authorization: apikey` header and the base URL;
  * checking a member search's parameters against the valid combinations before sending, raising `ArgumentError` for any other;
  * adding `program_id` to enrollment and consent create requests;
  * paging through `GET /api/members` and `GET /api/programs`;
  * Error classes per failure, such as `DataNexus::UnprocessableEntityError`, and `DataNexus::RateLimitError` with `retry_after`.

It installs from RubyGems.org with `gem "data_nexus", ">= 0.3"` in a Gemfile. `client.programs.list` needs version 0.3.0 or later. For example:
```
client = DataNexus::Client.new(api_key: ENV["DATANEXUS_API_KEY"], base_url: ENV["DATANEXUS_BASE_URL"])
program = client.programs.list(name: "Example Program").data.first
client.programs(program[:id]).search_members(born_on: "1976-07-04", employee_id: "ABC1234")
```

It covers programs (`GET /api/programs`); program members, including search (`/api/programs/{program_id}/members/search`), list, show, update and household; members (`/api/members`: list, show, update); and each member's enrollments (`/api/members/{member_id}/enrollments`) and consents (`/api/members/{member_id}/consents`): create, show, update and delete.


## About Dart Health

More info is available at [https://www.darthealth.com/](https://www.darthealth.com/).

## CHANGELOG (newest entries first):

* 2026-10-07 A failed enrollment create now says why. When the member or program is the problem,
its `422` body carries an `errors.code` of `no_prevailing_sponsor_member`, `program_not_found` or
`not_eligible_for_program`, where it previously said only "Unprocessable Content". Field and
request validation errors keep their shapes, with no `code`. The status is still `422`.
* 2026-10-05 The reference describes `data_nexus`, the Ruby client for this API, and the endpoints it covers.
Its server is now the path `/`, which resolves against the host that serves it.
* 2026-10-02 List Members (`GET /api/members`) is no longer deprecated.
* 2026-09-29 List programs now accepts the `first`, `last`, `after` and `before` paging
parameters and a case-insensitive `name` filter, and returns `has_next_page` and
`has_previous_page`. Invalid paging input returns 422. Show program now documents its
`data` wrapper.
* 2026-09-28 Member search now documents its result cap, that it cannot be paged, and what
`more_results` means.
* 2025-05-01 Member emails will now be provided as a list element, `emails`. We have deprecated `email` and
`work_email` but will provide them until the next major API version update.

422.description:
The enrollment was not created. The causes below all return `422`, so tell them apart by the shape of `errors`.

When `errors` is an object with a `code`, branch on the code:

* `no_prevailing_sponsor_member`: the member has no sponsor membership to enroll under.
* `program_not_found`: `program_id` is missing, no program has that ID, or the program is not available to this API key.
* `not_eligible_for_program`: the member's most recent sponsor membership has no active eligibility period for the program on the enrollment date. That date is the UTC date of `enrolled_at`, or today in UTC when it is absent. This is also the answer for another sponsor's program that this API key can see.

When `errors` is an object without a `code`, it maps field names to messages: the attributes were each valid but inconsistent, such as an `expires_at` before `enrolled_at`.

When `errors` is a list, the request did not match the request schema.

get.description:
Lists the programs your API key can see, ordered by name.

Results are paged by cursor. Without `first` or `last`, a page holds 25 programs. To read the next page, pass the response's `end_cursor` as `after`, and stop when `has_next_page` is `false`.

post.description:
Returns the program's members who match one combination of search criteria.

A search returns at most 10 members and cannot be paged: cursor and paging parameters are ignored. When more members match, the response sets `more_results` to `true`. Treat the list as incomplete, and narrow the criteria, for example by adding `employee_id` or the full first and last name, then search again.
